reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) describes the formation and benefits of nanocrystalline tribo-layers and glaze layers in a different alloy system (NiX), but none of it addresses laser remelting, Y2O3 coatings, or the CoCrFeNi HEA. The key premises about the specific intervention, material system, and quantitative performance predictions are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Laser remelting of a pre-deposited Y2O3 coating can produce a gradient nanocrystalline layer with uniformly dispersed nano-oxides in CoCrFeNi.
At room temperature, a refined nanocrystalline structure enhances hardness and limits shear band formation to reduce friction.
At elevated temperatures, embedded nano-oxides catalyze a dense, self-healing glaze layer that counteracts thermal softening and inhibits wear.
A dense, well-bonded nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear at high temperatures.
The proposed treatment will yield a 30–40% reduction in friction coefficient and an order-of-magnitude improvement in wear rate across the full temperature range.
